transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2025-03-05 15:00 PDT | Duration: 48 minutes | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Brooks (Redwood SE), Rajiv Menon (AtlasHealth CTO), Lina Gomez (Infra), Sasha Li (Privacy)

Summary: quick weekly sync; focus on pilot stability, perf regressions seen during long-run tests, and network config follow-ups.
Topics: performance numbers, KV cache tuning, VPC routing / NAT gateway behavior, runtime upgrade schedule, compliance asks.

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We should be at 48 minutes today, I think thats what we put on the calendar. Maya from Redwood here, Ethan joining to go through the results.
[00:15] Ethan Brooks: hey all, morning, afternoon — depending where you are. quick agenda: run through last week's benchmarks, network issues Lina flagged, upgrade plan for runtime 1.5.0, and open action items.
[00:35] Rajiv Menon: sounds good, thx. we had a couple of incidents during the long-run test on Thursday where tail latency spiked; want to understand root cause.
[00:50] Lina Gomez: yeah the 95th went up to ~480ms on one run, which is way above our target of 150 ms 95p. we think it coincided with a NAT gateway failover and some retry storms.
[01:05] Ethan Brooks: okay, that matches what we saw on the Redwood side. a couple notes: default keepalive settings on the customer LB + ephemeral NAT IP churn can cause session pinning issues and cold KV cache misses. we saw prefix cache hit drop to ~8% at the same time.
[01:25] Sasha Li: just to flag from privacy: any logging we turn on for deeper tracing, we need to confirm redaction/pseudonymization settings — we can't persist PHI in logs.
[01:40] Maya Patel: absolutely, Sasha. we've captured that in the compliance doc. i'll send the SOC2 evidence request list after the call.
[01:52] Ethan Brooks: quick perf recap: after last week's tuning (batch size adjustment and enabling prefix caching) steady-state 50p latency is ~65ms, 95p is ~180ms with current kv cache at 16GB. throughput holds at ~110 requests/sec on the pilot machine type.
[02:15] Rajiv Menon: 180ms is close but still above our SLO, correct? we are aiming for 95p <150 ms for patient-facing flows.
[02:30] Ethan Brooks: correct, target was 150ms. we think two levers give most lift: increase KV cache to 32GB to reduce cache miss penalty, and enable more aggressive batching for background routes where latency is less sensitive. also kernel-level optimizations in runtime 1.5.0 show about 10-15% latency improvement in our internal tests.
[02:55] Lina Gomez: for KV cache increase, we need to confirm disk and memory allocation on the node. current VM is using NVMe for spill, but we can allocate more ram—i'll check quotas.
[03:10] Maya Patel: noted. Ethan, do you have a recommended safe increment for KV cache? we want to avoid OOMs.
[03:25] Ethan Brooks: start with 24GB as a ramp step, monitor cache hit and eviction. increase to 32GB if stable. i'll include eviction thresholds and observability queries in the runbook.
[03:40] Rajiv Menon: regarding the NAT failover, Lina, what did we see in cloud infra? was it the cloud provider or our route table?
[03:55] Lina Gomez: we saw a failover of the NAT gateway; some outbound connections were re-synced to new ephemeral IPs and that caused a bunch of retries at the app layer. firewall had a short rule update too.
[04:15] Ethan Brooks: a practical mitigation is to use static egress IP via NAT gateway elastic IP and pre-approve those IPs in Redwood's firewall whitelist. we gave a list of Redwood egress addresses in the onboarding doc, but we can also support TLS mutual auth to avoid IP-based whitelisting.
[04:35] Maya Patel: i'll put that as an explicit action item — Lina to share NACLs and static IPs. we also recommended using longer TCP keepalives to survive brief NAT transitions.
[04:50] Sasha Li: on the mTLS note, is that currently supported in the Private control plane? we need mutual TLS for some regulated flows.
[05:05] Maya Patel: yes, mTLS is supported. Ethan can walk through cert rotation implications.
[05:15] Ethan Brooks: cert rotation works but we do recommend an overlapping rotation window — we present both old and new certs during the switchover. i'll write the steps.
[05:30] Rajiv Menon: ok good. next: runtime 1.5.0 — whats the plan and the risk surface?
[05:45] Ethan Brooks: 1.5.0 includes kernel improvements for attention kernels, some memory allocation fixes, and improved KV cache management. we saw a 10-15% latency reduction on 99% of workloads in internal bench. compatibility: quantized model artifacts need a small conversion step; models running under 1.4.2 will need an index rebuild.
[06:05] Lina Gomez: is that offline or will it require a full model reload / downtime?
[06:15] Ethan Brooks: you'll need a rolling restart of the inference pods; we support canary deploys to route a subset of traffic to the new runtime. no full data migration, but models may need a quick index warmup which we handle via pre-warm requests.
[06:35] Maya Patel: recommend a weekend maintenance window, run canary with 10% traffic for 1-2 hours, check latencies and error rates, then ramp. plan includes automatic rollback if 95p exceeds threshold.
[06:50] Rajiv Menon: can we do a test deploy in a sandbox beforehand? we'd prefer to validate with our integration tests.
[06:58] Ethan Brooks: yes we can spin up a sandbox cluster with identical configs. i'll provide terraform snippets and a checklist.
[07:10] Lina Gomez: on the sandbox, we need the exact runtime image tags and kernel args; please provide those.
[07:20] Ethan Brooks: noted, will send image tags and arg list post-call.
[07:25] Maya Patel: any new security/compliance asks from Sasha?
[07:30] Sasha Li: we need confirmation about log retention windows and whether debug traces can be disabled or filtered for PHI. also auditor access plan.
[07:40] Maya Patel: we've got a compliance pack, i'll attach the SOC2 summary. action: Sasha share specific audit checklist and i'll map required artifacts.
[07:52] Rajiv Menon: back to performance — you mentioned prefix caching changes last week. did those happen in-app or on the runtime side?
[08:05] Ethan Brooks: runtime side. we tuned prefix dedupe and increased default cache TTL which increased prefix hit rate from 18% to ~45% in short runs; that accounts for much of the steady-state improvement. but during the NAT failover we saw TTL expirations and evictions leading to spikes.
[08:25] Lina Gomez: if we increase TTL does that increase memory pressure?
[08:30] Ethan Brooks: yes, which is why the ramp to 24GB then 32GB is recommended. also if you enable NVMe spill, eviction cost goes up but less than a full model recompute.
[08:45] Rajiv Menon: are there any cost implications we should expect if we bump KV cache and run heavier batching?
[08:55] Maya Patel: yes there is a cost delta. i'll send a short delta estimate for Private vs Dedicated with the new resource profile. we can also simulate throughput to show cost per 1M tokens.
[09:10] Lina Gomez: re: routing — do you require specific peering or will internet egress from our private subnet work?
[09:18] Ethan Brooks: both are supported. peering (VPC peering or PrivateLink) is less brittle than public egress + IP whitelist. if you can do VPC peering, we prefer that for lower latency and no NAT.
[09:32] Rajiv Menon: we can open peering request with our network team; Lina will take that on.
[09:38] Sasha Li: for peering, we need to confirm cross-account IAM and also that logs stay in our account.
[09:45] Maya Patel: yes, peering keeps logs local. we'll document exact flow.
[09:52] Ethan Brooks: quick note on metrics: i'll add synthetic load tests and an example Grafana dashboard with the key queries. that will make the canary decisions repeatable.
[10:05] Rajiv Menon: great. any outage scenarios we need to plan for? earlier you mentioned graceful fallback to hosted model variants.
[10:15] Ethan Brooks: correct — if Private nodes are unhealthy, our router can fallback to a hosted variant with a different model size (e.g., from large to medium) while preserving semantics. for pilot you can opt-in to that fallback but i know for PHI flows you might not want external fallback.
[10:35] Sasha Li: we can't fallback to hosted for PHI workloads. need to keep within our VPC/control plane.
[10:40] Maya Patel: understood. we'll disable external fallback for the patient-facing route. we'll still exercise internal fallback policies like routing to other AZs or dedicated spare capacity.
[10:55] Lina Gomez: on backups for model indices, do you provide snapshots?
[11:02] Ethan Brooks: yes, we have model artifact snapshots and index backups; we can push backups to your S3 bucket if you want custody.
[11:12] Rajiv Menon: good. timeline: if we agree to the steps, can we aim to be in production by end of March?
[11:20] Maya Patel: end of March is ambitious but possible. primary gating: NAT/peering configuration, runtime upgrade validation, and SOC2 evidence. if we hit those, we can do a pilot cutover late March.
[11:35] Ethan Brooks: i'll prioritize the sandbox and the runtime checklist so you can validate early.
[11:42] Maya Patel: ok let's capture next steps and action owners.

Action recap (spoken):
[11:50] Maya Patel: Lina to share NACLs, firewall rules, and confirm static egress IP by 2025-03-07.
[11:58] Lina Gomez: yes I'll share that by Friday.
[12:02] Maya Patel: Ethan to deliver runtime upgrade plan, image tags, and rollback steps by 2025-03-10.
[12:10] Ethan Brooks: on it.
[12:12] Maya Patel: Sasha to send audit checklist and primary contact by 2025-03-11.
[12:18] Sasha Li: will do.
[12:20] Maya Patel: i'll send the updated runbook and cost delta by 2025-03-09 and SOC2 summary after the call.
[12:28] Rajiv Menon: we will schedule maintenance window for weekend of 2025-03-15 pending runbook review.

References shared: "Link: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/atlashealth-pilot"; "Runbook draft: internal/runbook-vpc-config.md"; "Sandbox terraform snippets: https://git.redwood/repo/pilot-sandbox"

[12:40] Maya Patel: anything else?
[12:45] Rajiv Menon: nothing from me. thanks all.
[12:48] Maya Patel: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the artifacts.

End of transcript.
